summary:
Small source-only research product recording a transport-configuration discrepancy as a lead; preflight-validated with valid=True and no diagnostics. No map change is proposed, so the accepted map and all accepted results keep their basis.

What was found: NetworkTransportConfig documents that 'For InstallSnapshot, we multiply the timeout by (SnapshotSize / TimeoutScale)' (net_transport.go:161-163), but that struct has no TimeoutScale field — it lives only on the transport itself (net_transport.go:109-110) — and NewNetworkTransportWithConfig unconditionally writes DefaultTimeoutScale into it (net_transport.go:226-238), ignoring anything a caller might expect to configure. The documented knob for scaling the snapshot send deadline is therefore inert through the public configuration struct; the only way to change it is to mutate the exported transport field after construction, which the snapshot sender reads directly in InstallSnapshot.

Kept as a lead rather than a Candidate because the consequence is a tuning gap for slow links or large snapshots rather than a protocol-safety issue, and raising Timeout itself remains an available workaround (though it widens every RPC deadline). Whether the ignored knob has ever caused an operational snapshot failure, and whether mutating the exported field is a supported path, are recorded as unestablished.

New sources: S64 (the config struct and its comment) and S65 (the constructor override). The feedback references existing objects only, so no new graph objects or versions were invented.

Run state: four confirmed in-scope violations with measured consequences for two of them, four reviews accepted with no pending work, and the remaining frontier unchanged — deployment-level reachability premises, the unmeasured duration/quorum consequences, the batching-FSM ConfigurationStore exemption, the snapshot tail lifetime under a live leader, the ReloadConfig and processHeartbeat leads, this new transport-configuration lead, and the still-unread in-memory snapshot store and observer plumbing.
